itinerary.cal: Boston Basin sites are won through NPS's early-access wilderness permit lottery (roughly 15% odds for the May 15-Oct 10 season).

days.note: Hike the climbers' path from the Cascade River Road trailhead through forest and boulder fields into Boston Basin, camping near 6,400 ft in the basin below the peak. An easy afternoon to sort gear and rack for the next day.
days.title: Approach to Boston Basin camp
days.objective: Establish camp in upper Boston Basin

days.note: Alpine start from camp, gain the East Ridge and follow ~8 pitches of low 5th-class rock to the true summit, then reverse over the summit block and downclimb/rappel the West Ridge to its notch and couloir back into Boston Basin. A full traverse avoids reversing technical terrain but makes for a long day.
days.title: East Ridge to summit, descend West Ridge (full traverse)

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Alpine start on the east side of the peak

schedule.label: Gain the East Ridge
schedule.detail: Start of the 8-pitch ridge climb

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Traverse to the true (west) summit

schedule.label: Begin West Ridge descent
schedule.detail: Downclimb/rappel to the West Ridge notch and couloir

schedule.label: Hike out (or camp a 2nd night)
schedule.detail: Most push out same day; some stay over and hike out the next morning

days.objective: Climb the East Ridge and descend via the West Ridge notch and couloir

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day trip: ~4 hrs / 2,800 ft hiking in to a Boston Basin camp, then a long 12-14 hr day climbing the East Ridge (8 pitches) and descending the West Ridge for a full ridge traverse, ~5,200 ft total gain.

road.name: Cascade River Road (Forest Road 15)
road.status: Gated at Eldorado Creek (MP 20) for the 2026 season following spring landslide damage near MP 18; bikes and pedestrians may pass the gate, but it is a further 3 miles and about 1,500 ft of road to the Cascade Pass trailhead. Reconfirm on the NPS Road Conditions page before driving.
road.seasonalGate: Normally gated at Eldorado Creek (MP20) through late autumn-spring.

days.note: Standard approach starts at the Beverly Turnpike Trailhead (3,600 ft), follows Trail #1391 then forks right up the Bean Creek drainage (1391A) to Earl Pass (6,200 ft) on the Bean/Standup Creek divide. From the pass, pick up intermittent tread on the southwest ridge and follow it up class 2 terrain to the 7,036 ft summit, with views to Mount Stuart and the Stuart Range. Descend by reversing the same ridge and trail.
days.title: Car-to-car via Bean Creek / Beverly Turnpike Trail and Earl Pass

schedule.label: Leave Beverly Turnpike Trailhead
schedule.detail: Trail #1391, then right fork onto 1391A up Bean Creek drainage.

schedule.label: Reach Earl Pass (6,200 ft)
schedule.detail: Steady climb with switchbacks as the trail steepens approaching the pass; designated tent sites here for parties who choose to camp.

schedule.label: Southwest Ridge scramble to summit
schedule.detail: Intermittent boot tread, class 2 scrambling on the ridge crest to the 7,036 ft high point.

schedule.label: Summit break
schedule.detail: Views of Mount Stuart, the Stuart Range, and on clear days Mount Rainier.

schedule.label: Descend, reversing the ascent route
schedule.detail: Ridge back to Earl Pass, then trail back down Bean Creek drainage.

schedule.label: Back at trailhead
schedule.detail: Total car-to-car time roughly 7-9 hours depending on pace and break length.

days.objective: Summit Earl Peak via the Southwest Ridge and return same day

itinerary.totalNote: A single long day car-to-car: about 7.5 miles round trip with 3,650 ft of gain, typically 7-9 hours including a summit break; no camping needed for the standard trip.

road.name: Teanaway Road (N. Fork Teanaway River Rd, paved to ~29 Pines Campground) to gravel FR-9737, then FR-9737-112 (Beverly Creek Road)
road.status: Closed to vehicles in 2026: FR-9737-112 washed out and is barricaded at the bottom, as the Cle Elum Ranger District's trail crew reported on September 25, 2026, and the Forest Service's Cle Elum road table dated September 8, 2026 also lists it closed. The trails beyond it are open again; walk the final mile-plus of the spur to the trailhead
road.driveNote: Turn right onto FR-9737-112 just before the road would cross Beverly Creek. In 2026 the spur is barricaded at the bottom after a washout, so park near the junction (room is tight by the bridge and the curves; never block the barricade) and walk its final mile-plus, a rough one-lane road, to the trailhead.
road.seasonalGate: Snow closure in winter/spring; in 2026 the FR-9737-112 spur is also closed to vehicles after a washout

itinerary.cal: No permit is needed for a day climb (only overnight camping in North Cascades NP requires one); Cascade River Road access and snow conditions on the ridge/glacier edge are the main seasonal gate, roughly July-September.

days.note: This is a long but standard single-day outing, not a backpack trip: parties drive to the Hidden Lake Trailhead (often sleeping at the trailhead the night before) and climb car-to-car via the Hidden Lake climbers' trail onto the ridge, then the East Ridge to the summit. Parties typically take roughly 6 hours up and ~10.5 hours round trip for a fit party, with a 4th-class step near the top and two 30 m rappels on the descent.
days.title: Car-to-car climb via Hidden Lake Trailhead

schedule.label: Leave Hidden Lake Trailhead
schedule.detail: Many parties camp at the trailhead the night before rather than hiking in early.

schedule.label: Reach climbers'-trail/ridge turnoff
schedule.detail: About 1 hour of trail hiking before leaving the maintained Hidden Lake tread.

schedule.label: Reach high saddle, start of East Ridge
schedule.detail: ~4.5 hours from the car via ridge and glacier-edge travel; crampons/axe useful depending on snow.

schedule.label: Summit East Peak
schedule.detail: ~6 hours car-to-summit; low-5th-class moves gaining the ridge are the technical crux.

schedule.label: Rappel the crux step, reverse ridge
schedule.detail: Downclimb exposed ledges and make two 30 m rappels off the ridge crest, then scramble back to the saddle.

schedule.label: Back at trailhead
schedule.detail: Total car-to-car time roughly 10.5 hours for a fit party.

days.objective: Summit The Triad's East Peak and return to the trailhead same day

itinerary.totalNote: A long single day, not a backpack trip: ~10.5 hrs car-to-car, 9.3 mi round trip, ~5,400 ft gain, via the Hidden Lake Trailhead and the East Ridge.

road.name: Cascade River Road (FR-15) to Sibley Creek Road (FR-1540)
road.status: Paved for roughly the first 10 miles from Marblemount, then gravel; FR-1540 (turnoff at about mile 10.2) is a rough 4.5-mile spur toward the small Hidden Lake Trailhead (~3,600 ft). FR-1540 is closed to vehicles by a washout at milepost 2.6 up the spur (Forest Service alert in effect since July 8, 2026, no end date given), adding several miles of extra road-walking each way to reach the trailhead. Even when clear, low-clearance sedans are not recommended, and the road cannot accommodate RVs or large trailers.
road.driveNote: A Northwest Forest Pass (or valid interagency equivalent) is required to park at the Hidden Lake Trailhead. Call the Mt. Baker Ranger District ((360) 854-2553) or check the NPS road-conditions page for the current FR-1540 washout status before driving.
road.seasonalGate: Typically clear of snow by late June or July and can close again with fall storms; also subject to flood/landslide closures -- verify current status with NPS before driving.

itinerary.cal: Within the July-September window, earlier is easier on the snow finger and gullies - by mid-to-late summer melt-out opens moats between snow and rock (especially in the west gully) and can add ice to the glacier traverse, making the route harder and slower.

days.note: From the Anderson-Watson Lakes trailhead (~4,300 ft), Trail 611 climbs steeply (~2.5 mi to a ~4,800 ft saddle above Watson Lakes) before the route contours south past Watson/Anderson Lakes and up open heather, rock slabs and talus to a camp with views of Baker and Shuksan. Expect a hot, buggy, sometimes overgrown trail early in the day and route-finding once the maintained tread fades near the lakes.
days.title: Backpack to high camp below Mount Watson
days.objective: Reach a camp around 5,400-5,600 ft on the open slopes below Watson's north side

days.note: Leave camp early for the short push to the ~5,900 ft col between Watson's East Peak and the true summit, then traverse the basin to the gully below the summit block. Parties report the west gully often holds a nasty moat/snow bridge later in the season, so most now take the more stable east gully; the final airy Class 2-3 summit block has real but short exposure. After tagging the top, reverse the route, break camp, and hike out.
days.title: Summit push via the east gully, then hike out

schedule.label: Break camp
schedule.detail: Quick breakfast, leave overnight gear staged or start packing it out.

schedule.label: Traverse to the col
schedule.detail: Rising traverse across heather/rock slabs to the ~5,900 ft saddle between the East Peak and main summit.

schedule.label: East gully
schedule.detail: Take the east gully over the west, which often has a moat/snow bridge by mid-summer.

schedule.label: Summit block
schedule.detail: Short Class 2-3 exposed scramble to the small summit; only room for a few people at a time.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Reverse the route back to camp.

schedule.label: Back at trailhead
schedule.detail: Full pack out after breaking camp.

days.objective: Tag the summit and return to the trailhead same day

itinerary.totalNote: A moderate 2-day trip: backpack roughly 4.5-5 miles to a high camp near 5,400-5,600 ft below Mount Watson, then scramble to the 6,221 ft summit via the east gully and hike all the way out the next day (~9-10 mi round trip, ~3,500-4,000 ft total gain); fit, fast parties compress the whole thing into a single long car-to-car day (~9-10 hrs).

road.name: FS Road 11 (Baker Lake Rd) to FS Road 1107 to spur FS Road 1107022
road.status: Paved Baker Lake Rd gives way to gravel FS 1107 and a rougher gravel spur (1107022) to the trailhead; normally passable to most passenger cars, but FS 1107 has been closed at a washout near milepost 3.8 — confirm current status before driving.
road.driveNote: The last stretch (1107022) is a narrow, unpaved spur road; go slow and watch for washboarding and potholes typical of late-season Cascade forest roads.
road.seasonalGate: Not gated, but the trailhead and route above it typically aren't fully snow-free until late June/July depending on winter snowpack.

road.name: Baker Lake Road (FR-11) to FR-1106/FR-1107, Anderson & Watson Lakes Trailhead
road.driveNote: FR-1107 (Anderson-Watson Road) has been closed at Mile Post 3.8 by a washout from the December 2025 floods (the road was already impassable in April 2026), with no end date given on the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest closure alert, issued July 8, 2026 and still posted on 25 September 2026 — this blocks vehicle access to the standard Anderson & Watson Lakes Trailhead. The shorter, brushier Bacon Creek Road (FR-1060) to spur NF-1064 on the mountain's SE side (~800 ft start) is closed too: the Forest Service's Electric Fire order (06-05-26-19) closes FR-1060 from SR 20 to NF-1064, and NF-1064 itself, from September 2 through October 31, 2026; verify current road/washout status before relying on either, as conditions change.
